title: Annotatio II NATIVITAS close crassior: Alger vs personal Impanation; stop before §.VI Ascelinus subtilior
pass_a_gloss: To Guitmund we rightly join ALGER, from Scholastic and Ecclesiastical a monk, demanding the same Impanation sentence as a new heresy in these words: Although, he says, the Sacrament is sufficiently distinct from the Thing of the Sacrament as figure from truth, yet certain erring ones say from certain words of the saints that Christ is so personally IMPANATED as God is personally incarnate in human flesh — which HERESY, because it is new and absurd, is to be rooted out by reasons and authorities.
pass_b_english: Alger joins Guitmund: some erring readers make Christ personally Impanated as God is personally Incarnate — a new absurd heresy to root out by reason and authority.
source_text: Guitmundo meritò adjungimus ALGERUM ex Scholastico & Ecclesiastico monachum, eandem Impanationis sententiam, novae hæreseos, hisce postulantem: Quamvis, inquit, Sacramentum à re Sacramenti tanquam figura à veritate satis distinctum sit, errantes tamen quidam, de quibusdam sanctorum verbis dicunt ita personaliter IMPANATUM Christum, sicut in carne humana, personaliter incarnatum Deum, quae HÆRESIS, quia nova & absurda est, rationibus & autoritatibus radicitus est exstirpanda.
